newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Nutricia's Milupa in new Salmonella-scare recall.
newsitem.headline: Nutricia's Milupa in new Salmonella-scare recall.

text.p: Dutch food group Nutricia on Monday faced a second product recall in a month, as its Milupa unit withdrew some batches of "Lemiel 2" baby formula in France because of concern over two cases of Salmonella poisoning.
The recall was a small-scale operation concerning only consignments of the product manufactured in July 1996 at Milupa's factory in Colmar, France, Nutricia said.

In January, Milupa withdrew its Milumil babymilk powder, manufactured at the same plant, from stores and clinics in Britain and Ireland because of a suggested link with the rare Salmonella anatum infection.
"During the incident in England, a statistical association was made between some Salmonella cases and the Milupa factory in Colmar," the company said.

"Further studies have showed that two Salmonella cases in France in September and October of last year had similar characteristics, on which basis the same relation to the Colmar factory could be made."
But no further Salmonella cases had subsequently arisen and tests of the Colmar factory, the product and raw materials had not revealed any contamination, Nutricia said.
The limited recall had been made after consultation with the French authorities, it added.

Nutricia's shares stood slightly lower on a mixed Amsterdam bourse at the midsession. The stock was briefly hard hit by the British recall in January, but has since powered back, setting a year-high of 280 guilders on Friday.
